name: Lincoln Quirk
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Product, Wave Mobile Money
profile: Co-founded Sendwave (low-fee US/UK-to-Africa remittances, sold to WorldRemit in 2020) and then Wave, a mobile money company that has grown into one of francophone West Africa's largest fintechs, starting in Senegal and valued around $1.7-2B. He met CEO Drew Durbin as a freshman hallmate at Brown and still leads product at Wave.
interesting_fact: Says he and his co-founders build Wave 'primarily for EA reasons'; he attended his first effective altruism gathering in 2013 (about 50 people in an Oakland house) and says he has had more impact through direct work at Wave than through donations.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2020 EA Forum AMA with CTO Ben Kuhn he said he personally wrote much of the original code for both Sendwave and Wave; Sendwave's pitch was sending money by phone number at a 3% fee vs the typical 8-12%.
notes: Low-profile; active in effective altruism circles (EA Forum). Best route likely via Wave or EA community. No published personal email found.

name: Shu Congxuan
current_role: Founder of Laoxiangji (Home Original Chicken), Hefei, Anhui (chairman in 2020; current formal title not confirmed)
profile: Former soldier who began raising chickens in Feixi, Anhui in 1982 and became one of the province's largest free-range chicken farmers. After a 1999 franchising course he opened the 'Feixi Old Hen' fast-food restaurant in Hefei in 2003, renamed Laoxiangji in 2012. The chain now has about 1,400 stores and has repeatedly attempted an IPO; his children hold most of the stake.
interesting_fact: In February 2020 he posted a video tearing up a letter in which employees offered to work without pay during COVID, saying he would sell houses and cars to keep about 16,000 staff fed and employed; it went viral and earned him the nickname 'China's best boss'.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army at 20 in autumn 1982, he spent his 1,800-yuan wedding money on about 1,000 chickens and reportedly ate and slept in the chicken shed for seven years while learning the trade.
notes: Chinese-language media only; reach via Laoxiangji corporate (Hefei). Reported to have transferred his direct shareholding to his children; daughter Shu Wen is an executive director.

name: Evan Doll
current_role: Rejoined Apple in 2016 as Director of Health Software Engineering (current role not confirmed by recent sources)
profile: Stanford 2003 grad who joined Apple as an engineer and worked on the original iPhone software (2003-2009). In 2010 he co-founded Flipboard, the magazine-style news app, with Mike McCue and led engineering/product; he left in 2015 for an EIR stint at Redpoint Ventures and returned to Apple in 2016 to direct health software engineering.
interesting_fact: Helped build the original iPhone's software as a senior iPhone engineer at Apple before leaving to co-found Flipboard, one of the breakout iPad apps of 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Healdsburg, California (Healdsburg High class of 1999, senior class president). While at Apple he taught an iPhone app programming class on the side and persuaded management to let him keep teaching: 'Teaching is a way to gain mastery.'
notes: Low public profile since returning to Apple; no recent interviews or published contacts. Apple employees rarely do outside media without Apple PR approval.
